physicalNotes: Radius 0.16683023 Jupiter radii from Heller et al. 2019 (2019A&A...627A..66H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...627A..66H/abstract): 11,927 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0131 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Heller et al. 2019 (2019A&A...627A..66H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname HELLER_ET_AL__2019): P 28.1656 d
sources.shape: Kruse et al. 2019 (2019ApJS..244...11K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KRUSE_ET_AL__2019): a/R* 61.5; Heller et al. 2019 (2019A&A...627A..66H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname HELLER_ET_AL__2019): inclination derived from its impact parameter 0.24 with the orbit's a/R* 61.5 (Winn 2010, eq. 7)
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Heller et al. 2019 (2019A&A...627A..66H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname HELLER_ET_AL__2019): transit mid-time 2456852.6572 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 579 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
